docs.title: Adaptify documentation
docs.text:
Adaptify helps insurance carriers get their products built, filed, approved and operational, all from one platform.

Adaptify is Insurance Product Lifecycle Management (IPLM). You manage each product's whole life in one place. Your forms, rates and rules live together, state by state. Changes run as projects, and approved work becomes your next release.

Start here: Get Started

docs.title: What's in Adaptify
docs.text:
• Product Vault: Governed repository for all products.
  • Project Workbench: Collaborative environment for building new products and updating existing products.
  • Filing Manager: Manage filings and objection handling all the way to approvals.

docs.text:

  • Bring a product into the Vault: from a new product to a published state in four steps.

docs.title: Filing Manager overview
docs.text: Filing Manager holds your filings being prepared for submission to regulators, from the first package to approval. Each filing covers one state. Filings are created when you complete a Workbench project as Admitted. See Complete as Admitted.

docs.title: Find a filing
docs.text:
1. Select Filing Manager in the left navigation. The Filings count shows how many filings you have.
  2. Use Search, Filters, Sort and Group to narrow the list.
  3. Open a filing. You can also open one from Active projects on the Dashboard.

A filing's name comes from its project and state, for example "Filing - Personal Auto fall update (Form, Rate) (AL)".

docs.title: What's on a filing page
docs.text: Area What it shows Path to submission A progress tracker for the filing. Filing package Not generated until you select Generate filing package, then Generated. Submission Not started until you record it with Manual submission, then the disposition, such as Pending or Approved. Objections tab The state's objections and your responses. Add one with + Add objection.

docs.title: Where each task starts
docs.text:
Task Start with Download the filing package (ZIP) for the state Generate filing package Record the date and SERFF tracking number Manual submission Log an objection and build your response Objections tab → + Add objection Record the state's decision The Submission status chip Close the filing and create the new release Archive project

The Release to New Release guide covers each task step by step. For what each status means, see Filing statuses and dispositions.

docs.title: Filing statuses and dispositions
docs.text: A filing page shows a status for its package, its submission and each objection.

docs.title: Filing package
docs.text: Status Meaning Not generated No package yet. Generated The package was built and downloaded as a ZIP with Generate filing package.

docs.title: Submission and disposition
docs.text:
You record the submission with Manual submission. The Disposition status then tracks the state's decision. To change it, select the status chip next to Submission, set Disposition status and the Change date, and save.

Status Meaning Not started The submission hasn't been recorded yet. Pending Submitted to the state and waiting on a decision. Approved The state approved the filing. You can now archive it with Archive project and create the new release.

The Disposition status list also includes Disapproved, Withdrawn, Closed and Noted. Choose the one that matches the state's decision.

docs.title: Approval type
docs.text:
You set the approval type for each state when you complete a project as Admitted, and it shows again when you record the submission.

Approval type Meaning Prior approval The state must approve the filing before you use it. File and use You file with the state and can use the filing once it's filed. Use and file You can use the filing first, then file it within the state's deadline.

docs.title: Objections
docs.text:
Status Meaning In Progress The objection is logged and your response is being prepared. Response submitted You built the response package for this objection.

Each response item shows Complete when it's done.

docs.title: Get Started
docs.text:
Adaptify Insurance Product Lifecycle Management (IPLM) is the operating system for P&C carriers.

Centralize forms, rules, rates, workflows and governance in one easy-to-use platform.

Use the left navigation to move between the areas below at any time. It also lists other areas, such as Reports and Bureau Circulars.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The Dashboard is the first page you see. It gives you a quick view of your projects, pending tasks and products.

  • The summary cards show Active projects, Pending tasks, Products in Vault and Total assets (forms and manuals).
  • Quick actions start common work: New project, Import product, Workflow management and Team management.
  • Your tasks lists your tasks, each with its type, time and status. Active projects lists the work underway.
  • Recent activity, below them, shows what's happened recently across your projects, such as a note added or a project moved to End. Choose View all to see more.

See Your Dashboard.

docs.title: Product Vault
docs.text:
Product Vault is a governed repository for all products. It's the single source of truth for your product assets.

  • The summary cards count your Products, Lines of business and Jurisdictions.
  • The Product catalog lists each product with its Status and Active work. Use Search products, Filters and Sort to find one, then open it to see its states and releases.
  • Choose Add product to add a product to the Vault.

See Product Vault overview.

docs.title: Project Workbench
docs.text:
Project Workbench is a collaborative environment for building new products and updating existing products.

  • The cards at the top cover the kinds of work: Form updates, Rate updates, Rules updates and New product.
  • Your projects are listed in the Project portfolio. Use Type to filter them, or turn on Show Archived Projects Only.
  • To start a project, choose + New project at the top right of the Project portfolio. Then choose Product update to update forms, rates or rules, or New product.
  • For a product update, pick Forms, Rates or Rules under Project type. Pick more than one to create a combined project with a child project for each type.

See Workbench overview.

docs.title: Filing Manager
docs.text:
Filing Manager lets you manage filings and objection handling all the way to approvals.

  • Filings shows each filing as a card with its state and status.
  • Once you have filings, use Search filings, Filters, Sort and Group to find one, then open it.

See Filing Manager overview.

docs.title: Adaptify at a glance
docs.text: Adaptify has three components. Together they cover a product from its current release, through an update and a state filing, to its next release.

docs.title: The three components
docs.text: Component What it's for Find it in the left navigation Product Vault A governed repository for all products: forms, manuals, rates, rules and supporting materials, state by state. Product Vault Project Workbench A collaborative environment for building new products and updating existing products. Workbench Filing Manager Manage filings and objection handling all the way to approvals. Filing Manager

docs.title: How a product moves through Adaptify
docs.text:
1. Start in the Product Vault. When you publish a product's states, they form its Baseline release, marked Current release.
  2. Start a project in the Workbench. Choose + New project, then Product update, and pick Forms, Rates or Rules. Pick more than one to create a combined project with a child project for each type.
  3. Move the work through phases. Each child project moves through Select, Review, Approve and End. Use Submit to hand it to the next person, with notes.
  4. Complete the project. Choose Complete project. Admitted creates a filing for each state in Filing Manager. Non-admitted completes the project without a filing.
  5. File with the state. In the filing, generate the Filing package and download the ZIP to submit in SERFF. Then record the submission, including Date submitted and SERFF tracking #.
  6. Handle objections. Add each objection the state sends on the filing's Objections tab, and track your response there.
  7. Approve and archive. Set the Disposition status to Approved. Then choose Archive project and Create new release. In the Vault, the new release becomes the Current release.

Release to New Release walks through steps 2–7 in detail.

docs.title: Your Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard is the first page you see after you sign in. Use it to see where your work stands and to pick up your next task. To get back to it, choose Dashboard in the left navigation.

docs.title: Read the summary cards
docs.text: Card What it shows Active projects Projects in progress. Pending tasks Tasks waiting to be done. Products in Vault How many products are in the Product Vault. Total assets (forms and manuals) Forms and manuals across your products.

docs.title: Start work from Quick actions
docs.text: Quick action What it opens New project Workbench, where you choose + New project to start a project. Import product Product Vault, where you choose Add product to add a product. Workflow management The list of your workflows, such as Product Update and Rate Update. Choose New workflow to add one. Team management Account management, with the tabs Overview, Users, Form numbering, AI configuration and Activity. Choose Add new user to add someone.

docs.title: Pick up your next task
docs.text: Your tasks lists the work assigned to you. Each row shows the item, its type (for example Filing), when it arrived (for example Just now) and its status (for example Pending). When you have nothing to do, it reads "You're all caught up". Choose View all to see more.

docs.title: See the work underway
docs.text: Active projects lists the projects in progress. When there are none, it reads "No active projects yet".

docs.title: Catch up on recent activity
docs.text: Recent activity sits below Your tasks and Active projects. Each entry says who did what, for example added a note, moved a project to End, created a project or archived a filing. Choose View all to see more.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Take a read-only tour of a product.
  • See how a product moves through Adaptify in Adaptify at a glance.

docs.title: Your first 10 minutes: tour a product
docs.text:
Take a read-only tour of one product, one project and one filing. You only look, so nothing changes.

Before you start: you need a product with a published release. Parts 4 and 5 also need a project and a filing; skip them if you don't have any yet.

docs.title: 1. Open a product
docs.text:
1. In the left navigation, choose Product Vault.
  2. In the Product catalog, open a product, for example Personal Auto.

docs.title: 2. Pick a state and a release
docs.text:
At the top of the product page:

  • Jurisdiction picks the state.
  • Release picks the version, for example Baseline.
  • Current release marks the release in use. New business and Renewal show its dates.

docs.title: 3. Look through the tabs
docs.text:
The tabs hold the product's assets for that state and release: Forms, Manual, Rates, Rules and Supporting Materials. Each tab shows a count.

  • On Forms, each row lists the form number and edition.
  • Shared · 2 marks a form used in two states.
  • Update marks a form changed in that release.
  • Rules lists the rules extracted from your manuals.

docs.title: 4. Open a project
docs.text:
1. In the left navigation, choose Workbench.
  2. In the Project portfolio, open a project.

A combined project shows how many child projects are complete, for example 0 of 2 complete, with the tabs Projects, Notes, Team and Activity. Open a child project to see which phase it's in.

docs.title: 5. Open a filing
docs.text:
1. In the left navigation, choose Filing Manager.
  2. Open a filing card.

The filing header shows the Jurisdiction, Filing type, Product, Target submission, Owner and Projects, and a tracker shows how many steps are ready. Under the Filing tab, Filing information shows the status of the Filing package and the Submission, followed by the forms and rates in scope. The other tabs are Objections, Notes, Team and Activity.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
That's the tour. Choose Dashboard to go back.

  • Learn how a product moves through Adaptify in Adaptify at a glance.
  • See what the Product Vault holds.

docs.title: Sign in and Org Setup
docs.text: You sign in with your email first, then your password. Everything you see after that (products, projects and filings) belongs to your organization.

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
1. Open the Adaptify sign-in page your organization uses. If you don't have the address, ask your organization admin.
  2. On Login to your account, enter your email under Email, then select Continue.
  3. Enter your Password and sign in. To check what you typed, select the eye icon in the field.
  4. The Dashboard opens and greets you by name: "Welcome back".

Typed the wrong email? On the password step, select the arrow next to your email to go back and change it.

Forgot your password? Select Forgot password? on the password step and follow the instructions.

docs.title: Confirm your organization
docs.text:
1. Check that the Dashboard shows the products and projects you expect.
  2. Your initials appear at the top right of every page.
  3. If you're an organization admin, your organization's name is at the top of System Administration → Account management.

If you don't see your organization's products, contact your organization admin.

Next: Your Dashboard.

docs.title: Clause, statute and objection libraries
docs.text:
The Intelligence group in the left navigation holds three libraries you can search while you build products and answer filings.

Library Use it to Guide Clause Library Browse the clauses in your forms, and start clause extraction from your published forms. Clause Library Statute Library Look up the statutes behind the compliance check, by state. Statute Library Objection Library Search past SERFF objections to prepare your responses. Objection Library

docs.title: Clause Library
docs.text: The Clause Library is where you browse clauses and place them in a section hierarchy, so you can find and reuse standard wording.

docs.title: Find a clause
docs.text:
1. In the left navigation, under Intelligence, open Clause Library.
  2. Check the summary cards: Clauses, Jurisdictions, Lines of business and Associated forms.
  3. Search with Search clauses by name or clause text.
  4. Narrow the list with Lines of business, or with Placement (All, Placed or Unplaced).

If nothing matches, you see "No clause found". Try another keyword or line of business.

To add a clause yourself, select + New clause.

docs.title: Extract clauses from your forms
docs.text:
Clauses come from your published forms. The Forms to process card shows how many forms are waiting.

  1. On the Forms to process card, select Start. The Clause extraction page opens.
  2. Find your product with Find a product or state, then select Process all for it (the button shows the number of forms).
  3. Adaptify parses each form. You review each one in Word, then the reviewed forms are extracted together.

The page tracks each form as Not started, Skipped, Parsing, To review, Reviewed or Extracted.

When new editions of your forms come in, the New editions card shows them. Select Open to see them.

docs.title: Objection Library
docs.text: The Objection Library holds past SERFF objections that states have raised. Look through it to see how a state has questioned similar filings before, and to prepare your response. It's read-only: you look things up and nothing changes.

docs.title: Find an objection
docs.text:
1. In the left navigation, under Intelligence, choose Objection Library.
  2. Look for objections like the one you're answering, and open one to read it.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: To answer an objection on one of your filings, add it to the filing's Objections tab. See Track objections and responses.

docs.title: Statute Library
docs.text: The Statute Library holds the tagged statutes behind the compliance check. Each row shows a statute's state, section, title, type of insurance scope and severity.

docs.title: Find a statute
docs.text:
1. In the left navigation, under Intelligence, open Statute Library. The Statutes count shows how many are in the library.
  2. Choose a State.
  3. Narrow the list with TOI scope (type of insurance) or Review status (draft or reviewed). TOI scope fills in once you choose a state. It's a searchable tree of types of insurance, starting with All P&C lines (wildcard), then codes such as 01.0 — Property and 04.0 — Homeowners.
  4. To find a specific statute, type in the search box (section, title, requirement or trigger summary), then select Search.

To see only the statutes flagged for a second look, turn on Needs review only. Rows that get mostly negative feedback are flagged needs review. Select Refresh to reload the list.

docs.title: What each column shows
docs.text: Column Shows State The state the statute belongs to Section The statute's section, as a link Title The statute's title TOI scope The types of insurance it applies to Severity / Verbatim How serious it is, for example HIGH or MEDIUM. Some rows also have a verbatim tag.

docs.title: Fix a statute's tagging
docs.text:
You can correct a row's line-of-business scope, severity or requirement. The next compliance run uses your change, with no re-tagging.

Statutes can't be added or imported here.

docs.title: Product Vault overview
docs.text:
Governed repository for all products.

The Product Vault (the Vault) is home base for every product you sell. Each state has its own tabs for forms, manuals, rates, rules and supporting materials. Process your documents, and Adaptify pulls rules from your manuals. Publish a state, and it gets its first release, the Baseline.

docs.title: At the top of the Vault
docs.text: The summary cards show how many Products, Lines of business and Jurisdictions are in the Vault.

docs.title: Find a product
docs.text:
Your products are listed in the Product catalog, with each product's Status and Active work.

  1. Select Product Vault in the left navigation.
  2. Use Search products..., Filters or Sort to find the product.
  3. Open the product.
  4. Choose a state under Jurisdiction. A status chip next to it shows where that state stands, for example Pending import or Processed.

In the Product catalog, each row shows the product's states and when it was last updated. Status shows where the product stands, for example Published or Pending Import. Active work shows any open Workbench projects, for example 1 project.

docs.title: What a product contains
docs.text:
Each state of a product has these tabs. The count on each tab shows how many items it holds.

Tab Holds Forms Policy forms and endorsements Manual Manuals, which the Vault reads to find your rules Rates Rate files Rules Rules extracted from your manuals Supporting Materials Supporting documents

When you publish a state, its files become the product's Baseline: the first release that later updates build on. See Review and publish.

docs.title: See every asset on a product
docs.text: To see all of a product's assets in one list, open the product and select Actions, then Asset summary. The Assets summary dialog has a tab each for Forms, Manuals, Rules and Rates. Each asset shows its status, for example Published, and the states it's used in. Draft assets that aren't used in any state can be deleted there.

docs.title: Bring a product in
docs.text: New to the Vault? Follow Bring a product into the Vault. It takes you from a new product to a published state in four steps.

docs.text:

  • Understand releases: Baseline, Current release, and how new releases arrive.
  • Shared assets across states: how one document is reused across states.
  • Fix a mistake: Delete a State or Delete Product.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: A few one-time setup steps make creating products in the Vault smooth.

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text: Sign in and confirm your organization first. See Sign in and Org Setup.

docs.title: Set up Group and Underwriting Company
docs.text:
Every product needs a Group and an Underwriting Company. Underwriting Company depends on Group, so each company must sit under a group.

  1. Go to System Administration → Lists.
  2. Create the Group value first.
  3. Open Underwriting Company and choose the Grouped by Group view.
  4. Select + Add value under {Group} and enter the company name.
  5. Reload the page and reopen Underwriting Company. The companies should still appear under the group.

Note

If the Underwriting Company field later shows No Options when you create a product, the companies are not linked to a group yet. Repeat the steps above.

docs.title: Check your product list
docs.text: Products are created from your tenant's product list (lines such as Personal and Commercial, and products such as Auto or Homeowners). Make sure the products you need are on the list before you create them. If one is missing, ask your organization admin.

docs.title: Bring a product into the Vault
docs.text: Here's how a product goes into the Product Vault (the Vault), in four steps. You can do them in one sitting.

docs.title: The four steps
docs.text:
1. Create a product. Give it a name, its lines of business and its states.
  2. Upload documents for a state. Add the forms, manuals and supporting materials for each state.
  3. Add metadata and process documents. Add form numbers and editions, then let the Vault read your files and pull out the rules.
  4. Review and publish. Publish each state so your team can start updating it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your Group and Underwriting company are already set up. Your organization admin does this once. See Before you start.
  • Have your files ready for each state:
Group File types Forms Word (DOC, DOCX) or PDF Manuals Word, PDF or Excel Supporting materials PDF

Use a file name of its own for each form

Give each form a file name that no other product in your Vault uses. Otherwise publishing the state can fail with "Failed to publish Product state". This is a known issue.

docs.title: Create a product
docs.text: Creating a product gives it a place in the Vault. You add its files in the next step.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Your organization admin sets up the Group and Underwriting company lists once. See Before you start.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Product Vault and select Add product. (On the Dashboard, Import product also takes you to the Product Vault.)
  2. Enter a Product name and a Description.
  3. Choose an Insurance type, Personal or Commercial, then choose the Lines of business.
  4. Choose your Group, then your Underwriting company.
  5. Under Jurisdictions, select every state the product needs. Double-check them before you save, for example AK, not AZ.
  6. Select Add product. You see "Product created successfully".
  7. Find the product in the Product catalog. Its status shows Pending Import, ready for its files.

When you open the product, its state reads "No releases yet — publish this jurisdiction to create its initial release." It gets its first release, Baseline, when you publish it.

Note

If Underwriting company shows No Options, its companies aren't linked to your Group yet. Ask your organization admin.

docs.title: Lines of business
docs.text:
Your organization's lists may differ. For example:

Insurance type Lines of business Personal Homeowners, Auto, Dwelling Property, Homeowners By Peril Commercial Builders Risk, Motor Truck Cargo, Inland Marine, Commercial Output

docs.title: Add product or a Workbench project?
docs.text:
Add product creates the product right away, with no Workbench project and no release yet. Use it when you have the product's documents ready to upload, process and publish yourself.

Made a mistake?

While none of the product's states is published, you can still delete it. See Delete Product.

Next: Upload documents for a state.

docs.title: Delete a State
docs.text:
Use this to fix a mistake, for example a state you added to the wrong product. It isn't meant for routine cleanup.

You delete a state in the Edit product dialog. There's no delete option on the Jurisdiction selector, in the Actions menu or in the Product Vault list.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Product Vault and open the product.
  2. Select Actions, then Edit product.
  3. Under Jurisdictions, select × on the state you want to remove.
  4. Select Save. A Please confirm dialog asks whether you want to delete the state.
  5. Select Delete. You see "Product updated", and the state is no longer listed under Jurisdiction.

This is permanent

Deleting a state permanently removes the product state and its documents. Assets still used elsewhere, and published assets, are kept.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
A product needs at least one state. If you remove its only state, Save stays unavailable.

To delete the whole product instead, see Delete Product.

docs.title: Delete Product
docs.text:
Use this to fix a mistake, for example a product you created twice or with the wrong details. It isn't meant for routine cleanup.

You can delete a product only while none of its states is published. Once a state is published, Delete product no longer appears.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Product Vault and open the product. Its states show pending import.
  2. Select Actions, then Delete product.
  3. The Delete product dialog says the product's forms, rules, rates and releases will be removed. Select Delete.
  4. You see a message that the product was deleted, and you're back in the Product Vault.

This can't be undone

Deleting a product removes its forms, rules, rates and releases.

docs.title: If a state is published
docs.text:
When a product has a published state, its Actions menu shows only Asset summary and Edit product. There's no way to delete it in the app. If you need a published product removed, contact Adaptify support.

To remove one state instead of the whole product, see Delete a State.

docs.title: Upload documents for a state
docs.text: You upload files one state at a time.

docs.title: Prepare your files
docs.text:
A simple folder for each state keeps uploads quick:

{Product}/{State}/Forms/                  DOC, DOCX or PDF
{Product}/{State}/Manuals/                PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS or XLSX
{Product}/{State}/Supporting Documents/   for the Supporting Materials tab

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open your product in the Vault and choose the state under Jurisdiction.
  2. On the Forms tab, select Browse files, or drag and drop your files. A form needs a Word file, a PDF, or both.
  3. On the Manual tab, upload the state's manuals. Rate manuals in Excel go here too.
  4. On the Supporting Materials tab, upload your supporting documents.
  5. Let each upload finish before you start the next one. Uploading one file at a time is the most reliable.
  6. Check that each tab's count matches your files.

The state shows Pending import until you process it.

If a count still shows 0

Refresh the page before you upload again. The count can lag behind the upload, and uploading the same form twice gives a "Duplicate form" error.

Use a file name of its own for each form

Give each form a file name that no other product uses. A repeated file name can block publishing later. This is a known issue.

Next: Add metadata and process documents.

docs.title: Understand releases
docs.text: A release is a version of a product's files for one state. Each state has its own releases, and the Current release is the one in use.

docs.title: When releases are created
docs.text:
• First publish: when you publish a state, it gets its Baseline release.
  • After an update: when an approved filing is archived with Create new release, the state gets a new release, for example Release 1. The new release becomes the Current release. Each state gets its own new release when its filing is archived.

docs.title: See a state's releases
docs.text:
1. In Product Vault, open the product.
  2. Under Jurisdiction, choose the state.
  3. Under Release, choose a release. Earlier releases, such as Baseline, stay in the list.

The header shows the release's New business and Renewal dates. The Current release chip marks the release in use.

docs.title: See what changed
docs.text: On the Forms tab, a form that changed in the release you're viewing shows an Update chip.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Start a product update

docs.title: Review and publish
docs.text: Publishing a state makes its files the product's Baseline release in the Vault, marked Current release. You need a published state before your team can update it in the Workbench.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Upload the state's files and add their metadata.
  • Run Process documents and check the Rules tab.

docs.title: Publish a state
docs.text:
1. In Product Vault, open the product and choose the state under Jurisdiction.
  2. Choose Review & publish. The Review and publish product panel opens.
  3. Check the cards for Manual, Rates, Forms and Supporting Materials. Each shows Files uploaded and Information pending. Information pending should be 0.
  4. Choose the Type of insurance. Then choose the Subtype of insurance, if one applies.
  5. Pick the New business effective date and the Renewal effective date from the calendar.
  6. Read the note This action cannot be undone, then publish.

The state's release now shows as Baseline with the Current release chip, and the dates you picked under New business and Renewal. Repeat for each state.

Dates

Pick dates from the calendar. Typed dates may not be saved.

docs.title: If you can't publish
docs.text:
• "Failed to publish Product state": check that no other product uses the same form file name. Upload the form with a file name of its own, then publish again.
  • A document's edition or title is locked: this can happen when a document is shared across states before its metadata is added. Add a document's metadata before you share it with other states.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Understand releases
  • Start a product update

docs.title: Shared assets across states
docs.text: When the same document is used in more than one place, for example the same form in Alabama and Alaska, Adaptify stores it once and marks it as shared. You can see the reuse at a glance.

docs.title: Spot a shared document
docs.text:
On a product's Forms or Manual tab, a shared document shows a Shared badge with a count, for example Shared · 2.

You'll also see the badge when you copy a state's forms to a new state in a Workbench project. The copied form then shows Shared on the product's Forms tab. See Copy a state's forms to a new state.

docs.title: Add metadata before you share
docs.text: Add a document's metadata, such as its form number and edition, before you use it in another state. Once a document is shared, its Edition and title can lock. If that happens, contact Adaptify support.

docs.title: Update a shared form
docs.text: You update a shared form in a Workbench project, like any other form. See Update forms. Adaptify starts the change as a draft. The shared document and its unique key stay unchanged until you publish.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Review and publish
  • Add a state to a product

docs.title: Add a state to a product
docs.text: There are two ways to add a state. Both are valid. Which one you use depends on whether you already have the product in that state.

docs.title: Which way to use
docs.text: Your situation Use Guide You already sell the product in the state, but the state was never added in Adaptify. Edit product in the Product Vault (Actions → Edit product) Add a state with Edit product You're expanding into a new state where you don't have the product yet. A Workbench project: + New project → New product → New jurisdiction for existing product Start a project to add a state, then Copy a state's forms to a new state

docs.title: Add a state with Edit product
docs.text: Use this when you already sell the product in the state, but the state was never added in Adaptify. If you're expanding into a new state where you don't have the product yet, start a project to add a state instead.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Product Vault and open the product.
  2. Select Actions, then Edit product.
  3. Under Jurisdictions, add the new state. The rest of the product's details are locked once a state is published.
  4. Select Save. You see "Product updated".
  5. Choose the new state under Jurisdiction. It's empty and marked pending import, with "No releases yet — publish this jurisdiction to create its initial release."
  6. Upload the state's documents on its page, or use Actions → Import forms, Import manuals, Import rates or Import supporting materials. See Upload documents for a state.

Until you publish the new state, the product shows Pending Import in the Product Vault's Product catalog.

The new state starts empty: no forms are copied from your other states. To start from another state's forms, start a project to add a state.

Note

You can't add a state from the Jurisdiction selector on the product page. It only lists the product's current states.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
Process and publish the new state like your first ones. See Add metadata and process documents and Review and publish.

To compare both ways, see Add a state to a product.

docs.title: Copy a state's forms to a new state
docs.text:
Use this to add a state to a product that's already in the Vault, starting from another state's forms, for example adding Alaska to Personal Auto from its Alabama forms. The new state starts with the source state's forms. You then review them, add the new state's own forms and publish.

Use this when you're expanding into a new state where you don't have the product yet. If you already sell the product in the state but it was never added in Adaptify, use Add a state with Edit product.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The product is published in the source state. See Review and publish.
  • This project copies forms only. Rates, manuals and supporting materials aren't copied (a known limitation).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In Workbench, choose + New project, then New product. For each wizard step, see Start a project to add a state.
  2. Product: under Product type, keep New jurisdiction for existing product.
  3. Project: under Project type, choose Forms.
  4. Configuration: under Product source type, keep Product Vault. Choose the Source product and the Source jurisdiction to copy from, for example Alabama.
  5. Source: choose the Target jurisdiction (for example Alaska) and the Type of insurance. Then in Finalize, enter the Project title, Project description, Workflow and Due date, and select Create project. The project opens with the source state's forms on the Forms tab, each with the change type Include.
  6. Check the copied forms. The source state's own state-specific forms, such as an Alabama amendatory endorsement, can be copied too. This is a known issue. Remove any form that only applies to the source state.
  7. Move the project through its phases with Submit. At End, choose Complete project, then the Non-admitted tab. Check the preview of included and new assets, then select Complete project.

In the Vault, the new state now has a Baseline release marked Current release. See Understand releases.

docs.title: Add the new state's own form
docs.text:
On the project's Forms tab, select Create form. In New document, keep New document under Document type. Enter a Form Number. When it says "Available. Use this number to lock it before continuing.", select Use this number. You see "Form number locked for this form." Add the Edition and Form Name, then select Add Form. The form is listed with the change type Addition.

New document takes the form's details only, with no file upload (a known limitation). See Add the product's documents.

In Complete project, you confirm with Complete project on the Preview.

To compare both ways, see Add a state to a product.

docs.title: Add metadata and process documents
docs.text: Processing turns a state's uploaded files into Vault assets, and pulls the rules out of your manuals. It needs a little information about each file first.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: The state's files are uploaded. See Upload documents for a state.

docs.title: The three steps
docs.text:
Do them in this order for each state:

  1. Add form numbers and editions. Each form needs its form number and edition.
  2. Add manual editions and set up rules. Each manual needs an edition, and Word and PDF manuals need their rule setup.
  3. Process documents and check the rules. Process the state, then check the rules that came through.

Add metadata first

Add every file's metadata before you process the state or use a file in another state.

Next: Review and publish.

docs.title: Add form numbers and editions
docs.text: Every form needs a Form Number and an Edition before you process the state. You enter them yourself. Processing doesn't fill them in from the file name.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the product, choose the state under Jurisdiction, and open the Forms tab.
  2. On a form, select the pencil icon to open its details.
  3. Enter the Form Number and Edition. These are the only required fields.
  4. Save your changes and close the dialog.

Repeat for each form. A form shows Metadata incomplete until its details are in.

docs.title: Read them from the file name
docs.text:
Form file names usually start with the form number, often followed by the edition, for example DEMO 0001 Personal Auto Policy.docx or DEMO 0002 09 20 Homeowners Policy.docx:

File name starts with Form Number Edition DEMO 0001 DEMO 0001 Not in the name: enter it from the form DEMO 0002 09 20 DEMO 0002 09 20

The form number is a prefix plus four digits. The edition is the month and year, as MM YY.

Next: Add manual editions and set up rules.

docs.title: Add manual editions and set up rules
docs.text: The Vault reads your manuals to find their rules. Give each manual an edition, then confirm how its headings are numbered. For most manuals, the default setup is all you need.

docs.title: Add the edition
docs.text:
1. Open the product, choose the state under Jurisdiction, and open the Manual tab.
  2. On each manual, select the pencil icon, enter the Edition, then save.
File name clue Edition 01 21, Rev 06 21 01 21, 06 21 Four digits at the end, such as 0823 08 23

docs.title: Set up rules
docs.text:
1. On the Manual tab, select Configure rules.
  2. On a Word or PDF manual marked Needs configuration, select Configure.
  3. Keep Configure manually and accept the defaults. The default Numbering style is Multi-level numbers with dots (1, 1.1, 1.1.2, ...).
  4. To use the same setup for other manuals, check them under Apply this configuration to other manuals.
  5. Select Save, then Done.

Leave Excel manuals (.xls files) alone. You don't need to configure them.

Set up rules before you process

After a state is processed, Configure rules can become unavailable. This is a known issue, not how it's meant to work. Set up every manual first.

Add editions early

Add a manual's edition before you use it in another state. A manual shared across states can lock its Edition if you add the edition afterwards, and that blocks publishing. This is a known issue.

Next: Process documents and check the rules.

docs.title: Process documents and check the rules
docs.text: Processing reads the state's files and pulls the rules out of your manuals. Afterwards, check the rules before you publish.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Every form has its form number and edition. See Add form numbers and editions.
  • Every Word or PDF manual has its edition and rule setup. See Add manual editions and set up rules.

docs.title: Process the state
docs.text:
1. Open the product and choose the state under Jurisdiction.
  2. Select Process documents once.
  3. If you're told a manual isn't configured yet, cancel and set it up first. A manual processed without its rule setup may give you no rules.
  4. Wait for processing to finish. Uploads and edits pause while it runs. Refresh the page to see the status move from Processing to Processed.

docs.title: Check the rules
docs.text:
1. Open the Rules tab and expand the tree, for example 1 MANUAL FORMAT → 1.1 Multistate Rules Manual.
  2. Check that each manual's headings came through with their numbers and titles in order.
  3. If rules are missing, check that manual's edition and rule setup on the Manual tab.

Check the rules, not just the count

The Rules count can change after you edit metadata, and it doesn't always match the rule tree. Some titles can also come through wrong, for example a page number from a manual's index. These are known issues. Look at the rules themselves before you publish.

Next: Review and publish.

docs.title: How rating works in Adaptify
docs.text:
Rating is how your approved products become operational. A rater works out the premium for a product. In the Rating Catalog, each rater ties a product and one of its jurisdictions to the rating structure it's built on.

You build a rater in five parts, in this order:

Rating structure → Rating tables → Calculations → Rate order → Tests

Part What it is Where Rating structure Every risk item, coverage and field your rating uses, such as Policy, Location, Zip code or Protection Class. Rating Administration → Rating structure. See Rating structures. Rating tables Your rate and factor tables. Each column is linked to a field in the structure. The rater's Tables tab. See Rating tables. Calculations The steps that turn table values and inputs into premium, drawn as a flow. The rater's Calculations tab. See Calculations. Rate order The order Adaptify runs the calculations in. The rater's Rate order calculation tab. See Rate order. Tests Test cases with an expected premium, so you can check the rater gives the right answer. The rater's Manual tests and Test suites tabs. See Test a rater.

docs.title: Start with the structure
docs.text: Everything your rating uses to develop the rate lives in the rating structure. Set it up first: tables and calculations can only use fields that are already in the structure.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Rating structures
  • Open a rater

docs.title: Calculations
docs.text: Calculations turn your table values and rating inputs into premium. Each calculation is a flow you draw on a canvas, step by step.

docs.title: Find or start a calculation
docs.text:
1. Open the rater and choose the Calculations tab. It has two views: Risk item calculation and Coverages.
  2. Choose the Risk item, such as Policy, then the Risk item calculation. Its flow appears on the canvas.
  3. To start a new one, select + Create new. In Create new risk item calculation, enter the Risk item calculation name, choose the Risk item, then select + Create new risk item.

You can also Delete, Copy or Edit the calculation that's open.

docs.title: What's on the canvas
docs.text:
Every flow runs from START to END. In between, you link these nodes with arrows:

  • Table: looks up a rating table.
  • Calculation: a set of math steps.
  • Branch: a condition that sends the flow one way or another, such as checking for a wind exclusion. Each path can have a label.

Select Edit to change the flow. Add nodes from the palette on the left, then link them.

docs.title: Configure a calculation
docs.text:
Open a Calculation node to configure it.

  1. Enter a Name.
  2. Under Add Functions, choose a function. It's added to Steps. Functions include +, -, *, /, ROUND, ROUND_UP, DAYS_BETWEEN, MONTHS_BETWEEN, YEARS_BETWEEN, YEAR, IF, FOR_EACH and TABLE_LOOKUP.
  3. Fill in each part of the step. For each one, choose a Binding Type:
    • Step: the result of an earlier step.
    • Path: a field from the rating structure, picked from Select Path.
    • Value: a number you type in.
  4. Select Save.

For example, step 1 could be Fire Peril Base Rate × Fire Territory Factor, and a later step could round the result.

If a part is still empty, you'll see "Values are missing for one or more functions". Fill it in before you save.

docs.title: Configure a branch
docs.text: Open a Branch node to set its condition in Configure Condition: give it a Name, build the IF condition, then add what happens under THEN and ELSE.

docs.title: Check your work
docs.text: Open the rater's Actions menu and choose Validate.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Rate order

docs.title: Open a rater
docs.text: In the Rating Catalog, select the rater's row in the Rater catalog to open it.

docs.title: What's on a rater
docs.text:
• Breadcrumb: Rating Catalog and the product's name. The product name is also the rater's title.
  • Jurisdictions: the state you're working on, for example AL.
  • Version number: the version, for example Baseline, with its status (such as Draft) and effective date.
  • Actions: Create new version, Publish, Import, Export and Validate.

docs.title: The six tabs
docs.text: Tab Use it to Guide Tables Build and fill in your rating tables. Rating tables Rating structure See the structure the rater is built on, and pick an item to view its fields. Rating structures Calculations Draw the calculation flow for each risk item or coverage. Calculations Rate order calculation Set the order the calculations run in. Rate order Manual tests Create test cases one at a time and run them. Test a rater Test suites Run batches of tests from a spreadsheet. Test a rater

docs.title: Rate order
docs.text:
The rate order is the order Adaptify runs your calculations in. Open the rater and choose the Rate order calculation tab.

The calculations are numbered and grouped by risk item, such as Location and Policy. Use Search and Type to find one. Select Edit to change the order. Until a rater has calculations, the tab reads "No calculations found".

docs.title: Get the order right
docs.text:
• Put the tables before the calculations that use them.
  • Put Total Premium last.

When you're done, open the rater's Actions menu and choose Validate.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Test a rater

docs.title: Rating Administration and rating structures
docs.text: A rating structure lists every risk item, coverage and field used to develop the rate. You set it up in Rating Administration, before you build tables and calculations.

docs.title: Open your rating structures
docs.text:
1. Select Rating Administration under Rating in the left navigation. You'll see two cards: Rating structure and Rating APIs.
  2. Choose the Rating structure card. The Rating structures list opens.

Each structure in the list shows its name, a status badge (Draft or Active), Insurance type, Line of business and Effective date.

docs.title: Create a rating structure
docs.text:
1. On Rating structures, select + New rating structures.
  2. In Add new rating structure, enter the Name and Description, and pick the Effective date.
  3. Choose the Insurance type, then the Line of business. All five fields are required.
  4. Select Add rating structure. You'll see "Rating structure created successfully", and the new structure opens as Draft with a single Policy item.

docs.title: What's on a structure
docs.text:
• Header: the name, status badge, description, and the Insurance type, Lines of business and Effective date. Edit and Actions are at the top right.
  • Rating structure: the tree of risk items and coverages, starting with Policy. Each item shows its cardinality, Single or Multi. Use Search structures and fields to find one.
  • Applicable fields: select an item in the tree to see its fields. Fields used as rating inputs show an Input tag, and rating outputs show an Output tag.

docs.title: Add risk items and coverages
docs.text:
1. In the Rating structure panel, select Edit. The tree switches to edit mode and the button becomes Exit edit.
  2. Select Add on the item you want to add under.
  3. In Add new item, choose the Type (Risk item or Coverage), and enter the Name and Description.
  4. Choose the Cardinality and an Icon, then select Add. You'll see "New item created successfully".
  5. Select Exit edit when you're done.

Use Multi for things a policy can have more than one of, such as several locations or vehicles, scheduled personal property or coverages. Use Single for everything else.

docs.title: Build the structure in Excel
docs.text:
For a big structure, building it in Excel saves time.

  1. On the structure, open Actions and choose Export in XLSX.

  2. Fill in the file. It has a sheet for each part of the structure, such as Policy, Location and each coverage. Each sheet lists its fields in these columns:

    Column What to enter Field Name The field, for example Zip code or Protection Class. Data Type Number (decimals are fine), String or Boolean. Dates use Date. Sequence Number The order the field appears in on the test input screen. Leave gaps, such as 10, 20, 30, so you can slot new fields in later. Rating Input TRUE if you need to enter this value to rate, for example Zip code or Protection Class. Rating Output TRUE only if you want to see the value in the output, for example Territory.

  3. Back on the structure, open Actions and choose Import in XLSX, then pick your file.

Actions also has Import in JSON and Export in JSON.

docs.title: Change the structure's details or status
docs.text: Select the header Edit to change the Title, Description, Status (Active or Draft), Insurance type, Lines of business or Effective date. Then select Save changes.

docs.title: Missing a field?
docs.text:
If you find a field is missing while you build a table, add it to your structure file and import it again here. Then go back to your table. Fields always come from the structure, so your tables and structure stay in step.

Tip

Keep your structure file open while you build tables, and import again whenever you add a field.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Open a rater

docs.title: Rating tables
docs.text:
Rating tables hold your rates and factors, such as base rates, territory factors or age of home factors. Each column is linked to a field in the rating structure, so Adaptify knows what to look up and where to put the result.

Open the rater and choose the Tables tab. The Rating tables panel lists the tables. Use Search tables to find one, then select it to view it. Input and output columns are marked with different icons.

docs.title: The Manage menu
docs.text:
Select Manage next to Rating tables to:

  • Add new table, Import table, Import tables, Import tables from manuals or Export all tables.
  • Under Actions for selected table: Export table, Copy table, Edit table details or Delete table. Select a table first.

docs.title: Add a table
docs.text:
1. Select Manage → Add new table.
  2. Enter the Name and, if you like, a Description.
  3. Choose the Type: None or unspecified, Premiums, Loss costs, Factors or Relativities.
  4. Enter the Rule number, if there is one.
  5. Select Add table. The new, empty table opens.

docs.title: Set up the columns
docs.text:
1. Select the table, then select Edit.
  2. Select New Column. The Edit column panel opens.
  3. Enter the column's Name.
  4. Choose the Column type: Input for a value you look up by, such as Zip code, or Output for the value you get back, such as Territory.
  5. For an input column, choose the Column conditions: Equals, Greater Than, Greater Than or Equal To, Less Than, Less Than or Equal To or Interpolate.
  6. Under Select path, search for and pick the structure field this column maps to. It fills in the Risk item field, for example Policy.Vehicle.Territory, and shows its Data type.
  7. Select Save. Add the next column the same way.
  8. Select Save changes to save the table, or Cancel to discard your changes. Undo and Redo step through your edits.

docs.title: Fill in the table
docs.text:
While you edit the table, select a cell to type a value into it, then select Save changes. For a large table, it's quicker to use a file:

  1. Select Manage → Export table. You get a CSV file with the column headers.
  2. Fill in the rows in Excel and save it as CSV.
  3. Select Manage → Import table, then choose your CSV file.

docs.title: Add the table to a calculation
docs.text: Add each new table to your Calculations. That's what brings it into the rate order and your tests.

docs.title: Test a rater
docs.text: Test a rater by entering rating inputs and comparing the premium Adaptify works out with the premium you expect.

docs.title: Create a test case
docs.text:
1. Open the rater and choose the Manual tests tab.
  2. Select Create test case.
  3. In Add new manual test, enter the Test case name and the Expected premium, then select Add test. You'll see "Test case added successfully".

Each test case in the list has Export, Copy, Edit and Delete. You can also Import test cases from a JSON file exported from manual tests, or Export all.

docs.title: Run a test
docs.text:
1. Open the test case. You'll see the Expected Premium and Actual Premium.
  2. On Rating Inputs, fill in the inputs. These are the fields marked as rating inputs in the structure, in sequence-number order. Use the Policy tree on the left to move between risk items.
  3. Select Execute Test. A message tells you whether the test passed, with the premium.

Give every required input a value, then run the test.

docs.title: Read the Rate Log
docs.text:
Choose Rate Log to follow the math step by step. It shows exactly how each premium was worked out.

  • The list on the left shows each calculation, grouped by risk item.
  • For each table lookup, you see the Input and Output: the field, its path and its value.
  • For each calculation, you see each step with the numbers filled in and its result.
  • For each branch, you see the IF, THEN and ELSE, with the path that was taken.

Use the filters at the top, such as Risk Item, Coverage and Node Type, to narrow the log.

docs.title: Test suites
docs.text:
To run a batch of tests from a spreadsheet, use the Test suites tab:

  1. Select Download template and fill it in.
  2. Select Create test suite, enter the Test suite name, choose your file (XLSX, XLS or CSV), and select Create. You can also use Import with template.

Each suite shows how many of its tests passed and failed, its file, when it last ran and its status.

docs.title: Rating Catalog
docs.text:
The Rating Catalog is where approved products become operational. It lists all the raters built on your products and rating structures. Each rater ties a product and one of its jurisdictions to the rating structure it's built on.

Open it from Rating Catalog under Rating in the left navigation.

docs.title: What you'll see
docs.text:
• Summary cards: how many Raters, Jurisdictions and Rating structures you have.
  • Rater catalog: the list of raters, with a count. Add rater is at its top right.

docs.title: Filter and sort the list
docs.text:
Above the list, use:

  • Insurance type: All, Personal or Commercial.
  • Lines of business: narrow the list to a line of business. Each filter has a search box.
  • Sort by: Alphabetically (A-Z) or Alphabetically (Z-A).

docs.title: Add a rater
docs.text:
A rater is built on a rating structure, so the rating structure you want must exist before you start.

  1. In the Rater catalog, select Add rater.
  2. Choose the Product. The list shows the products in your Product Vault.
  3. Choose the Jurisdiction. It's available once you've picked a product.
  4. Choose the Rating structure the rater is built on.
  5. Select Create. It's available once all three fields are filled in.

Next, open a rater to build it. For how the pieces fit together, see How rating works in Adaptify.

To see how a product moves through Adaptify, see Adaptify at a glance.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Terms used in Adaptify and in these docs are collected in one place.

  • Glossary: admitted and non-admitted, filing, release, project, and the other words these guides use.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Terms you'll see in Adaptify and in these docs, in alphabetical order.

  • Admitted / Non-admitted: The two ways to finish a Workbench project with Complete project. Admitted creates a filing for each state in Filing Manager. Non-admitted completes the project without a filing.
  • Archive project: The last step on an approved filing. Choosing Create new release while archiving makes a new release of the product in the Vault.
  • Baseline: The first release of a product's state, created when you publish it with Review & publish.
  • Child project: One project inside a combined project, for one project type: Forms, Rates or Rules.
  • Combined project: A Product update that covers more than one project type. It holds a child project for each type.
  • Current release: The label on the release in use for a product's state.
  • Disposition status: The state's decision on a filing's submission, for example Pending or Approved.
  • Filing: The Filing Manager record for one state's submission, created when you complete a project as Admitted.
  • Filing package: The ZIP of a filing's documents that you generate in Filing Manager and submit to the state through SERFF.
  • IPLM: Insurance Product Lifecycle Management: managing a product from concept through its operational life in one place.
  • Jurisdiction: A state the product is sold in. Use the Jurisdiction picker on a product page to switch states.
  • Manual: The product page tab for rating and rules manuals. Adaptify extracts rules from them.
  • Objection: A question or issue the state raises about a filing. You add and track objections and your responses on the filing's Objections tab.
  • Phase: A stage in a Workbench project: Select, Review, Approve and End. Use Submit to move work to the next phase.
  • Prior approval: An approval type you can choose when you complete a project as Admitted and when you record a submission.
  • Process documents: The Vault action that turns uploaded files into product assets and extracts rules from your manuals.
  • Product update: A Workbench project that updates the forms, rates or rules of a product that's already in the Vault.
  • Release: A version of a product's assets for one state, for example Baseline. Use the Release picker on a product page to switch versions.
  • SERFF tracking #: The tracking number from SERFF that you record on a filing's submission.
  • Shared: A badge on a document used in more than one state, for example Shared · 2.
  • Supporting Materials: The product page tab for supporting documents.
  • Update: A badge on a form that changed in a release.

docs.title: Release to New Release
docs.text: Use this path when a product that's published in the Product Vault needs changes to its forms or rates. You update the product once, file it state by state, and each state's approval becomes that state's new release.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The product is published in each state you want to change, for example with a Baseline release. See Review and publish.
  • Your organization's filing workflow and owners are set up. If you're not sure, ask your organization admin.

docs.title: The path
docs.text:
Product Vault (current release) → Workbench project → one filing per state in Filing Manager → Product Vault (new release)

  1. Update your product in Workbench: change forms and rates in one project.
  2. Create filings from your project: complete the project as Admitted to get one filing per state.
  3. Add documents and supporting materials to each filing, as the state requires.
  4. File with the state and record the submission: download the ZIP, file in SERFF, and record it.
  5. Track objections and responses: log the state's objection and your response.
  6. Record approval and archive to a new release: mark the filing Approved and create the new release.
  7. Check the new release in the Product Vault: confirm each state shows its new release as current.

Each state moves on its own

Each state's filing is submitted, approved and archived separately. One state can reach its new release while another is still answering an objection.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Start with Update your product in Workbench.

docs.title: Record approval and archive to a new release
docs.text: Do this when the state approves the filing. Archiving the approved filing creates that state's new release in the Product Vault.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. On the filing, choose the Pending chip next to Submission.
  2. Set Disposition status to Approved and pick the Change date from the calendar. Save. The submission shows Approved. See Filing statuses and dispositions.
  3. Choose Archive project.
  4. In Archive project, check the Destination product state (product and state). Under Release association, choose Create new release. The Release version fills in for you.
  5. Enter the New business effective date, the Renewal effective date and a Description, then archive. A success message appears.
  6. Repeat for each state's filing.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Example Release version Filled in for you, for example 1 New business effective date 12/01/2026 Renewal effective date 12/01/2026 Description Fall 2026 forms and rates update

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Check the new release in the Product Vault

docs.title: Check the new release in the Product Vault
docs.text: Do this after you archive each state's filing. The Product Vault now shows the new release as that state's current release.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Product Vault and choose your product, for example Personal Auto.
  2. Under Jurisdiction, choose the state. Release shows the new release, for example Release 1, with the Current release chip and the New business and Renewal dates you entered.
  3. On the Forms tab, updated forms show an Update chip, for example Update AL.
  4. To see the earlier version, choose an earlier release, such as Baseline, under Release. See Understand releases.
  5. Repeat for each state.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Your product's states are up to date. The next time the product changes, start again at Release to New Release.

docs.title: Create filings from your project
docs.text: Do this when every child project in your Workbench project is complete. Completing the project as Admitted creates a filing for each state in Filing Manager. For more about this dialog, see Complete as Admitted.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the combined project and choose Complete project.
  2. Choose the Admitted tab.
  3. Under Destination states, check that each state you're filing in is listed, for example Alabama (AL) and Alaska (AK).
  4. For each state, fill in Approval Type (for example Prior approval or File and use) and Owner.
  5. Review the summary. It groups the changes by state and shows each Asset, its Change and its Scope. Then confirm.
  6. Open Filing Manager. Each state now has its own filing, for example "Filing - Personal Auto – Fall 2026 forms and rates update (Form, Rate) (AL)".

Field Example Approval Type Prior approval Owner Your filing owner

Pick any dates from the calendar. Typed dates may not be saved.

If a state doesn't need a filing, use the Non-admitted tab instead. See Complete a project.

docs.title: Track objections and responses
docs.text: Do this when the state sends an objection letter about a filing. Each objection gets its own page, where you build and track your response.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • Save the state's objection letter as a PDF.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. On the filing, open the Objections tab and choose + Add objection.
  2. Enter the Objection number and pick the Response due date from the calendar. Drag in the objection letter or choose Browse files, then choose Add objection. The objection shows In Progress.
  3. Open the objection. Its page has Response items, Forms and Supporting documents.
  4. Add a response item: enter a Description and choose a Preparer, then choose + Add item.
  5. Choose View response package, then Download ZIP, and send your response to the state. The objection shows Response Submitted. For what each objection status means, see Filing statuses and dispositions.

docs.text: Where Field Example Add objection Objection number OBJ-01 Add objection Response due Pick from the calendar Add objection Objection letter (PDF) Objection letter.pdf Response item Description Provide support for the liability rate change Response item Preparer A team member

docs.title: Next
docs.text: When the state approves the filing, go to Record approval and archive to a new release.

docs.title: File with the state and record the submission
docs.text: Do this when the filing is ready to go to the state. You file in SERFF, outside Adaptify, then record the submission in Adaptify.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In Filing Manager, open the state's filing. Under Filing information, choose Filing package.
  2. The Generate filing package dialog lists the Forms and Rates in the filing. Choose Download ZIP. The filing package shows Generated.
  3. Outside Adaptify, upload the ZIP to SERFF and submit it. Note the SERFF tracking number.
  4. Back on the filing, choose Manual submission to open Record submission.
  5. Enter the details in the table below. Approval type carries over from the Workbench project, and Disposition status stays Pending. See Filing statuses and dispositions.
  6. Save. The submission shows Pending, with your SERFF tracking number and the date you submitted.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: If the state sends an objection, see Track objections and responses. If the state approves, go to Record approval and archive to a new release.

docs.title: Update your product in Workbench
docs.text: Do this when a published product needs new editions of its forms or rates. One Workbench project can cover forms and rates for every state you're changing.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In Workbench, choose + New project, then Product update. For each step in detail, see Start a product update.
  2. Setup: under Project type, choose Forms, Rates or both, then choose Next. If you choose both, you get one combined project with a child project for each type.
  3. Configuration: choose the Product and the Jurisdictions, for example Personal Auto in Alabama and Alaska. Choose Next.
  4. Finalize: enter the Project title and Project description, check the workflow for each type, and pick a Due date from the calendar. Choose Create.
  5. Open the forms child project and choose Add form. In Add form changes, choose Update form, select the forms, enter the Updated edition (for example 01 27) and choose Change. In the rates child project, do the same under Add rate changes with Update rate. See Update forms and Update rates.
  6. Move each child project forward with Submit. Choose a person under Select Assignee, add a Due date if you want one, and enter Add notes. Form projects move through Select, Review, Approve and End. Rate projects move from Select to End.

When every child project reaches End, the combined project shows that all its projects are complete.

Keep the description short: only the first 100 characters are kept.
